text:
maria: quick RFC follow-up — we sketched three ways to account for tokens when a request falls back from a paid/pinned model to an open/compatible model. want to lock an approach before the rollout tomorrow.
alex: can you list the options again? i skimmed but want the tradeoffs called out.
maria: sure — short version: (A) bill against original model's quota but route to cheaper model (absorbs cost on us), (B) bill actual model used (tenant pays for cheaper), (C) hybrid: bill original but annotate refund/credit if fallback used a lot. each has fairness/abuse implications.
sam: A is simplest for callers (predictable), but opens a vector: clients could intentionally request premium models then design prompts that trigger fallbacks to save money while retaining routing benefits.
lee: B seems clean economically but breaks SLAs/expectations: customers pin a model for quality, if we silently run cheaper model and charge them less, they might be surprised by quality regressions and then dispute.
alex: hybrid (C) is intriguing — we keep a predictable charge, and if fallback rate crosses a threshold we issue credits or force explicit downgrade. what threshold?
maria: proposal in RFC was 10% fallback over a 1h window as a guardrail. above that we either require explicit downgrade or start tagging responses as degraded.
ops-bot: automated signal: fallback_rate=12.4% tenant=acme-corp window=60m — alert sent to #customer-success
sam: that alert is doing its job. still, enforcement matters. If we issue credits retroactively, it can be gamed by starting/stop requests around windows.
lee: plus refunds are operationally messy. i'd rather implement a policy that forces non-stealth downgrade: if fallback_rate > 10% we switch routing to a visible fallback-mode for that tenant and surface a banner in console + email.
alex: agree. visibility helps trust. And we should add telemetry: per-request model_tag + fallback_reason so CS and infra can triage.
maria: ops: timeline? we need a light-weight change for tomorrow: add per-request model_tag and count fallback_rate; for enforcement we can do console banner + opt-in billing reconciliation next week.
sam: implementation notes: modify ingress router to attach header `X-Model-Effective` and `X-Model-Requested`, store both in telemetry. small DB counter per-tenant windowed metric.
lee: watch out for bursty patterns — use an exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) or sliding window? EWMA is cheaper but less explainable.
alex: prefer sliding window with max resolution 1m buckets — easier to debug for customers.
maria: agreed: 1m buckets for 2h retention. then EWMA for internal quick reacts if we want faster gating.
ops-bot: checklist created: [x] router headers, [ ] metrics pipeline ingestion, [ ] UI banner, [ ] billing reconciliation path
sam: abuse mitigation question: if a tenant is intentionally requesting premium then forcing fallbacks to exploit latency/capacity, do we protect other tenants? we need a protective backpressure policy.
lee: propose tenant-level soft cap on fallback throughput that decays gracefully and triggers graceful shed when others hit SLO. basically credit a fallback budget separate from normal quota.
alex: that ties into admission/lease layer — we should add a fallback-burst-budget that we decrement on each fallback request; exhausted -> probabilistic reject or queue.
maria: high-level decision: implement (C) hybrid with visibility first, add fallback-burst-budget and tenant banner for >10% fallback, and do retroactive credits only on manual review (no automated refunds for now).
sam: sounds good. follow-ups: write a tiny RFC stub for the fallback-budget shape + counterexamples to avoid gaming.
lee: i'll draft the RFC and include the probe patterns that would detect gaming. ping @maria when ready.
alex: i'm on the router header patch — will open PR in 30m. tagging infra to prioritize metric ingestion.
maria: thanks all. sync in the morning if anything blocks the rollout. :thumbsup:
